findings: All six formal and nine pilot configurations use batch size one; naive within-batch node-count normalization would equal the present loss.
The hinge zeros a currently wrong target's own loss contribution, not a permanent mask based on its clean prediction.
Size-proportional replacement sampling has a size-weighted hinge expectation at fixed parameters, not an identical zero-one MR objective.
Both historical pilots remain negative under both descriptive summaries; no trained uniform-replacement control was run in those nine pilots.
Target and candidate identities are disjoint within a current group; cross-group reuse is not proof of leakage.
Holding the first target identity fixed does not hold its contextualized Transformer representation fixed.
Equal budget caps do not prove equal realized injected-node/edge counts.
Degree matching does not automatically preserve the paper's unique-neighbor budget or its global average.
Constrained membership swaps are neither implemented nor proven uniform/well mixed.
An evaluation-method extension still requires owner direction and confirmation that it satisfies course requirements.
changes_before_publication: Added the contextualized-representation limit to the proposed first-target control.
Required actual injected-node/non-self undirected-edge accounting, preserved mismatches and unchanged denominators.
Required an explicit paper-budget average population and source-order preservation checks before protocol freeze.
